From: Aaron Chen <aaron.chen@theiahealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent disconnects during long-lived sessions

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing a pattern in production where our SDK clients (v1.3.2) that hold long-lived streams to Redwood endpoints drop the connection after ~6-8 minutes under load. That causes our pipeline to restart and double-request in a few places. I attached a small trace (handshake_trace_20270331.txt) showing the TLS re-handshake and a sequence of RSTs.

Can your team help confirm whether this is expected behavior (connection TTL / keepalive policy) or whether the SDK/runtime mismatch might be causing premature connection closures? We’re trying to avoid a full switch to short poll if we can — long-lived streaming is important for latency and cost for us.

We’re happy to provide more logs or a repro harness. This is on our US region cluster and is blocking part of our pilot.

Thanks,
Aaron
Aaron Chen
Senior Platform Engineer, Theia Health

Attachment: handshake_trace_20270331.txt (text)

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connection lifecycle constraints — initial runtime notes

Quick triage notes after running the trace:

- Observation: the external trace shows a TLS ClientHello followed by a delayed ServerHello and then an immediate close (RST) from the client side after ~6-7 minutes of inactivity on the wire. The timing lines up with our connection_reap_idle default (6m).
- Hypothesis: the runtime’s ephemeral connection reaper is closing underlying socket when route-level idle thresholds are reached; SDK does not attempt graceful reconnect with request idempotency, so the caller restarts the request.
- Short repro path: reproduce with a single client keeping a streaming request idle for 7 minutes then send a small payload. I can run this locally if Theia provides a minimal repro harness.

What I need from platform/runtime to confirm:
1) Exact value and logic for route-level idle reaping in us-west-2 (config path: runtime.conn_reaper.*).
2) LB (edge) logs for the same window — to know if reaper or LB reset.
3) Telemetry on connection close reason (if we have ECONNRESET vs application close).

Proposed *short-term* workaround: bump conn_reaper.idle_ms to 900000 (15m) for the pilot corridor for Theia (config hotfix), and add a client-side SDK option (keepalive_interval) that sends a small ping frame every 3–4 minutes. The client ping avoids the reaper and is low-risk.

I can draft the config change and a quick SDK snippet for Aaron to test. Estimated time: 1 day to draft + 2–3 hours to deploy hotfix to canary pool.

-Dev

Attachment referenced: repro-snippet.patch (I’ll attach the snippet in follow-up)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connection lifecycle constraints — runtime perspective

Thanks Dev — good catch. Quick notes from runtime kernel side:

- Confirmation: default conn_reaper.idle_ms is 360000 (6m) for the public cluster. This was set conservatively to avoid socket buildup under high fan-out.
- Impact assessment: bumping to 900000 for a narrow pilot looks low risk if we scope to Theia's CIDR (we can do routing policy by customer tag).
- Longer-term ask (product / SDK): we should expose a documented SDK flag for multiplexed stream keepalives (e.g., sdk.keepalive.send_ping_ms) and a server-side opt-in header (X-Client-Keepalive) so runtime knows to skip the reaper for tagged connections. This avoids changing global defaults and is safer for multi-tenant clusters.

Workplan suggestion:
1) Short-term: Dev to propose config patch for pilot + we deploy to canary (ETA 1 day). Lauren to approve external communication.
2) Mid-term (3–4 sprints): Product to accept feature request to add SDK keepalive config + runtime header opt-in. Runtime will implement polite skip-of-reaper for tagged connections; product must sign off on security/abuse surface and telemetry.
3) Sales: offer Theia a one-week pilot extension and rollback credits if performance slips during the config window.

Jonas
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
